items.title: CL-winnaar Pacho bespreekt 'donkere periode': 'Een wond die nooit heelt'
items.summary: Willian Pacho heeft in aanloop naar de strijd om Europese Super Cup tussen Paris Saint-Germain en Aston Villa teruggeblikt op een emotionele periode in zijn leven. Waar het leven hem nu vooral toelacht, met onder andere de Champions League-winst in mei, daar kende de Ecuadoriaan op jonge leeftijd donkere dagen na het overlijden van zijn moeder.

items.title: ‘It is just smelling football’: Tielemans says adjusting to life at United has come naturally
items.summary: Midfielder says experience has helped him settle in ‘It’s what I’ve been doing from when I was young’ Youri Tielemans has stated that adjusting to Michael Carrick’s vision for Manchester United has been as easy as “smelling football” for the vastly experienced £35m midfield signing. The 29-year-old, who joined from Aston Villa last month, made his debut for Anderlecht at the age of 16. He has been integrating with the United squad during the past 10 days of the club’s pre-season tour, making his first appearance in Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg. Continue reading...

items.title: I owe Villa the world but Man Utd are above them - Tielemans
items.summary: Manchester United new boy Youri Tielemans gives his first extended interview on his £35m dream move, making it third time lucky for the ex-Aston Villa man.

items.title: Barcelona make improved £51m bid for Rodri as Manchester City target Fernández
items.summary: Latest offer close to City’s valuation for Spain midfielder Chelsea’s £120m price for Fernández may be too high Barcelona have made an improved bid to Manchester City of around €60m (£51m) for Rodri. This follows Barça’s initial offer of €45m that was rejected out of hand by City. The Spanish club’s new offer – which may include add-ons – is close to City’s valuation for the 30-year-old who captained Spain to the World Cup and won the Ballon d’Or in 2024. As the midfielder has declared a preference for Barcelona it seems it is inevitable he will leave. In preparation City are targeting Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández as a potential signing though the west London club’s valuation of around £120m may be too high. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘It’s a nice hobby’: Manchester United’s Janina Leitzig on goalkeeping and gardening
items.summary: Former Leicester player’s focus has moved from runner beans to running drills as the season approaches With some parts of England gearing up for a fifth heatwave of 2026, the new Manchester United goalkeeper Janina Leitzig, a keen gardener, is sympathetic to the precarious health of this reporter’s tomato plants. “You’re not used to so little rain, are you?” she observes. For the time being, after her summer move to Manchester, the former Germany youth international does not have a garden of her own, but she reveals that, during her three-and-a-half-year spell at her former club Leicester, homegrown vegetables were her pride and joy. “I love to do some gardening. Back home, everyone has their own vegetables and it’s just better, it tastes better,” she tells the Guardian. “Being away from home and away from family, of course you have your football friends, but still it can be quite lonely sometimes if you come home from training, so it was really nice to have a garden and to spend time outside. It’s not too much effort, it’s just a nice hobby.” Continue reading...

Club Brugge toonde verregaande interesse in Abdoulie Manneh, maar Cercle Brugge handelde sneller en wist op die manier de winger nu ook in huis te halen. items.title: Saudi Pro League tries to move on from era of ageing megastar but big names still loom
items.summary: As Ronaldo heads towards 1,000 career-goals, league plans to lift standard of Saudi Arabian football, not just the clubs There’s no Mohamed Salah in the new Saudi Pro League season that kicks off on Thursday and while the age of the ageing megastar is ending, there is still the strong chance that the next few months will be dominated by Cristiano Ronaldo. The 41-year-old is 24 shy of 1,000 career goals and with the five-time Ballon d’Or winner having scored 102 in 107 league games for Al-Nassr so far, the milestone could – should – be reached this season. Huge as that will be, just how it fits into the plans of the league is unclear. This is the fourth season since the spending started with $957m (£710m) splashed out in that summer of 2023. It delivered thousands of articles, dozens of international broadcasting deals and untold numbers of people worldwide sporting the yellow CR7 Al-Nassr shirt. Now, though, the focus is on getting a little more value for money and lifting not just the clubs but the standard of Saudi Arabian football in general. Continue reading...
